rationale: Neuroimaging analysis from the index cohort describing SPG93 (Kaiyrzhanov et al., 2022) identified 19 affected individuals harboring bi-allelic NFU1 variants, of whom 16 displayed the milder, prolonged-survival spastic paraplegia spectrum (ranging from pure spastic paraplegia to complex HSP forms). Across the cohort, white matter abnormalities on brain MRI were documented as invariable (100% penetrance), including in individuals initially presenting with pure early-onset spastic paraplegia before episodic febrile neurological decompensations or progression to complex neurology. Independent reports (e.g., Safka Brozkova et al., 2026; Mahmoud et al., 2025) and clinical ontology databases corroborate that cerebral white matter changes (gliosis, volume reduction, leukoencephalopathy) are a consistent signature of NFU1-related spastic paraplegia. No counter-examples reporting completely normal cerebral white matter on neuroimaging in confirmed SPG93 have been published to date.

evidence.text: Kaiyrzhanov et al. reported 19 individuals from 10 families with bi-allelic NFU1 missense variants presenting with a spectrum ranging from pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (16/19 individuals with prolonged survival) to severe neurodevelopmental delay with hypotonia (3/19), explicitly noting invariable cerebral white matter abnormalities on neuroimaging across the cohort.

new_directions.question_text: At what chronological age or disease stage do white matter abnormalities first appear in asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic NFU1 variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether white matter abnormalities precede motor signs or appear simultaneously during early neurodevelopment is critical for assessing MRI as a true preclinical predictive biomarker.

new_directions.question_text: What specific qualitative neuroimaging features (e.g., cavitating leukoencephalopathy, corpus callosum thinning, or periventricular sparing) reliably distinguish SPG93 from other recessive spastic paraplegias such as SPG11, SPG15, or SPG35?
new_directions.rationale: While white matter involvement is invariable in SPG93, many other complex HSPs also present with leukodystrophy-like changes; detailed radiological scoring would improve differential diagnostic specificity.
